questions.question: She ___ in a bank in Kraków.
questions.explanation: Present Simple: w 3. osobie liczby pojedynczej (he, she, it) dodajemy -s: she works.

questions.question: We ___ at home yesterday evening.
questions.explanation: Przeszła forma to be: I/he/she/it was, ale we/you/they were.

questions.question: There ___ two apples on the table.
questions.explanation: There are + liczba mnoga (two apples); there is + liczba pojedyncza.

questions.question: ___ your brother play the guitar? – Yes, he can.
questions.explanation: Odpowiedź „Yes, he can” pokazuje, że pytanie jest o umiejętność: Can your brother play…?

questions.question: Look! The children ___ in the garden.
questions.explanation: Look! – coś dzieje się teraz: Present Continuous. Children to liczba mnoga, więc are playing.

questions.question: I usually ___ breakfast at 7 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Posiłki: have breakfast / lunch / dinner. „Robić śniadanie” w sensie przygotować to make breakfast, ale „jeść” to have.

questions.question: My mother's brother is my ___.
questions.explanation: Brat mamy albo taty to uncle (wujek). Cousin to kuzyn, nephew – bratanek albo siostrzeniec.

questions.question: I'm hungry. Can I have a ___ of pizza?
questions.explanation: Kawałek pizzy albo ciasta to a piece of. Glass, bottle i cup to naczynia na napoje.

questions.passage: Hi! My name is Marta. I'm from Gdańsk, but now I live in Kraków with my sister. I'm a student. I don't have a car, so I go to university by bike. At the weekend I visit my parents.
questions.question: How does Marta get to university?
questions.explanation: W tekście: „I go to university by bike”. Samochodu nie ma (I don't have a car).

questions.passage: Dear Tom, I'm sorry, but I can't come to your party on Saturday. My grandma is ill, and I'm going to visit her with my dad. She lives in Poznań, so we're leaving early in the morning. Have a great time! I'll call you on Sunday. Love, Ania
questions.question: Why can't Ania go to the party?
options: She has to work on Saturday.
She is going to Poznań with her friends.
questions.explanation: Chora jest babcia, nie Ania: „My grandma is ill, and I'm going to visit her”.

questions.question: I ___ a great film last weekend.
questions.explanation: Konkretny czas w przeszłości (last weekend) → Past Simple. See jest nieregularne: see – saw – seen.

questions.question: This exercise is ___ than the last one.
questions.explanation: Krótkie przymiotniki (także zakończone na -y) stopniujemy przez -er: easy → easier than.

questions.question: I ___ here since 2019.
questions.explanation: Since + punkt w czasie: sytuacja trwa do teraz → Present Perfect (I have lived).

questions.question: If I had more free time, I ___ another language.
questions.explanation: Second Conditional (sytuacja nierealna teraz): If + Past Simple, would + bezokolicznik.

questions.question: If she had left earlier, she ___ the train.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional (przeszłość, która się nie wydarzyła): If + Past Perfect, would have + 3. forma.

questions.question: The lights are off. They ___ gone to bed already.
questions.explanation: Pewny wniosek o przeszłości: must have + 3. forma (na pewno już poszli spać).

questions.question: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the documents.
questions.explanation: Po Not only na początku zdania stosujemy inwersję z operatorem: Not only did he arrive…

questions.question: ___ I known about the delay, I would have taken a taxi.
questions.explanation: Okres warunkowy bez if: Had I known… = If I had known… (Third Conditional z inwersją).

questions.question: The committee recommended that the proposal ___ postponed.
questions.explanation: Subjunctive po recommend / suggest / insist that: forma podstawowa be bez względu na osobę i czas.

questions.question: ___ as it may seem, the experiment was a complete success.
questions.explanation: Fronting z as: przymiotnik + as + podmiot + may/might + czasownik (Strange as it may seem = choć może się to wydawać dziwne).
